title: Illuminating the dark kinome utilizing multiplex peptide activity arrays to functionally annotate understudied kinases

predicted_errors.supporting_evidence: The figure and its embedded table label the kinase as 'EPHA8' (e.g., 'EPHA8 | 27%', 'EPHA8_Medium Affinity'), but the paper studies EPHA6. This is a mislabeled panel/table and contradicts the text that reports EPHA6.

Fig. 2C is cited twice for mutually exclusive content: first for concentration-dependent signal intensity ('Signal intensity of phosphosites with increasing total protein ... (Fig. 2C...)'), and later for amino-acid sequence logos ('We visualized the amino acid sequence logos ... (Fig. 2C...)'). One panel cannot be both the dose-response curve and the sequence logos.

The text states samples were 'spun down at 13×G for 15 min at 4°C.' A centrifugation force of 13×g is essentially gravitational and cannot pellet homogenized tissue; this should almost certainly be 13,000×g. As written the protocol is impossible.

predicted_errors.error_location: Methods, postmortem tissue kinome profiling and LFC calculation
predicted_errors.supporting_evidence: The study pooled samples by diagnosis and sex ('control (17...) and schizophrenia (16...)'; 'Pooled samples were run in technical triplicate') and then computed LFCs and upstream kinase enrichment across those technical replicates. This destroys subject-level biological replication and treats technical replicates as biological replicates, so the schizophrenia-vs-control statistical comparisons are pseudoreplicated and cannot support the reported disease-kineome conclusions.

predicted_errors.error_location: Methods, upstream kinase analysis using BioNavigator
predicted_errors.supporting_evidence: The experiment uses a PTK PamChip ('phosphotyrosine (PTK) chips'), but the upstream kinase analysis says the 'standard STK analysis protocol' was used. The default STK protocol is for serine/threonine kinases, not tyrosine kinases, so using it for PTK-chip data is internally inconsistent and likely an incorrect analysis setting.

The text states predicted functional pathways were examined using 'three approaches: co-expression clustering, protein–protein interaction networks, and genetic perturbation analysis,' but only the first two approaches are described. No genetic perturbation analysis is reported in the visible results, making the stated three-approach description internally incomplete/contradictory.

The abstract claims '195 novel kinase-substrate interactions' were identified, but the evidence is in vitro phosphorylation of immobilized reporter peptides on a PamChip. Peptide phosphorylation by a recombinant kinase does not establish a bona fide kinase-substrate interaction, and most hits were not validated. The stated number also does not obviously match the summed peptide-hit counts in the text (65+53+15+5+63=201 peptide-kinase combinations), so the claim overstates the biological meaning of the screen.
